Mohan Singh
--Petitioner
 Versus
Competent Authority
--Respondent
Hon’ble Pankaj Purohit, J.
Ms. Priyanka Agarwal, learned 
counsel for petitioner.
2. Mrs. Mamta Bisht, learned Dy.A.G 
with Mr. Devesh Ghildiyal, learned Brief 
Holder for the State.
3. The petitioner has challenged the 
order dated 27.08.2026 passed by 
respondent no.1 whereby the petitioner’s 
application under Section 3H (4) of the 
National Highways Act, 1956, has been 
rejected saying barred by limitation.
4. It is contended by the learned 
counsel for petitioner that respondent
no.1 has no right to decide the 
application, which reflects dispute of the 
apportionment of amount or part thereof 
and to whom the same is payable, rather 
it should refer the dispute for decision to 
the Principal Civil Court of original 
jurisdiction within which the land is
situated.
5. Learned counsel for the petitioner  contends that impugned order dated 
27.08.2026, by which petitioner’s 
application was decided by respondent 
no.1-Cala, is totally in violation of law
and cannot be sustained.
6. Issue notices to the respondent nos. 
2 to 4 returnable within three weeks.
7. Steps to be taken within two days.
8. List this case on 30.11.2026, after 
fresh.
9. In the meantime, the respondent 
nos.2 to 4 are restrained from changing 
the nature of property.
 (Pankaj Purohit, J.)
 02.11.2026
Nahid
